theme: The anointing; the Supper; Gethsemane; arrest
readingInstruction: Read Mark 14:1-52. The plot, the anointing at Bethany, the Last Supper, Peter’s predicted denial, Gethsemane, and the arrest. Notice the contrast between the woman’s love and Judas’s betrayal, and between Jesus’ prayer and the disciples’ sleep.
settingTheScene: It is two days before Passover. The chief priests are looking for a way to arrest and kill Jesus quietly. Mark again sandwiches stories: the plot frames the anointing, and Peter’s predicted denial frames the Supper and Gethsemane. Mark’s account is the most raw: the disciples all flee, and a young man runs off naked. This is probably Mark himself.
observation: “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a beautiful thing to me” (14:6).
“This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many” (14:24).
“You will all fall away, for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered” (14:27).
“Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will” (14:36).
“Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak” (14:38).
“And they all left him and fled” (14:50).
interpretation:
In Bethany, a woman breaks an alabaster flask of costly nard and pours it on Jesus’ head. Some are indignant at the waste, saying it could have been sold for three hundred denarii, nearly a year’s wages. Jesus says, “Leave her alone. She has done a beautiful thing to me.” She has anointed his body beforehand for burial. “Wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will be told in memory of her.” Right after this, Judas goes to the chief priests and offers to betray him.

At the Passover meal, Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him, one who is eating with him. They are sorrowful and ask, “Is it I?” He takes bread, blesses it, breaks it, and says, “Take; this is my body.” He takes the cup, gives thanks, and says, “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.” This is the covenant sacrifice, like Moses sprinkling the blood at Sinai (Exodus 24:8). He will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until the day he drinks it new in the kingdom of God. They sing a hymn and go to the Mount of Olives.

On the way he says that they will all fall away, quoting Zechariah 13:7. Peter insists, “Even though they all fall away, I will not,” and Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows twice, he will deny him three times. Peter says even more vehemently that he will not deny him, and they all say the same.

In Gethsemane, Jesus is “greatly distressed and troubled” and says, “My soul is very sorrowful, even to death.” He falls to the ground and prays, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will.” Abba is the intimate word for Father. The cup is the wrath of God against sin. Jesus does not want to drink it, and yet he submits. He returns three times to find the disciples sleeping. “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” Then: “The hour has come. The Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.”

Judas arrives with a crowd armed with swords and clubs and gives a signal: “The one I will kiss is the man.” He kisses him. They seize him. One of the bystanders draws a sword and cuts off the ear of the high priest’s servant. Jesus says, “Have you come out as against a robber?” and that this is to fulfill the Scriptures. Then, in Mark’s sad phrase, “they all left him and fled.” Jesus is utterly alone.
connection: Exodus 12 and 24:8 are the Passover and the covenant blood. Jeremiah 31:31-34 promised the new covenant. Zechariah 13:7 is the shepherd struck. Psalm 41:9 predicts the betrayal by a friend. Isaiah 53:5-12 describes the servant who is pierced and who pours out his soul to death. Psalm 42:5-6 and 116:3 are cries of a soul in distress. Romans 8:15 and Galatians 4:6 say we cry “Abba” by the Spirit. Hebrews 5:7-8 recalls his prayers with loud cries and tears.
application:
Pray “Abba, Father” today and let the word sink in. You are his child.

When you face a hard obedience, pray Jesus’ prayer: “Yet not what I will, but what you will.”

Remember that the Lord’s Supper proclaims his body broken and blood poured out. Receive it with thanks.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the cup Jesus drank for you.
Thank him for the blood of the covenant poured out for many.
Pray, “Abba, Father,” and tell him what you want to give him.
